I got tired of sending people a raw broker link and calling it a funnel.

So I put the process I actually use on a page:

• stake planner (account × risk %)
• daily loss limiter
• a 20-trade sample counter

They run in the browser. No login. They do not place trades.

If $500 at 1% risk does not look exciting, that is the point. Exciting stakes are how accounts vanish in a bad week.

Volatility 75 does not close.

That is useful for practice. It is also why people sit in front of 1-second ticks like it is a night shift.

A salary has hours. This market does not. You have to put the clock on yourself: session length, trade cap, daily stop. Otherwise there is always one more tick that looks like getting even.

I wrote that up without a secret setup, because I do not have one worth selling.

Three trades is a mood. Twenty is a sample.

After two losers the brain wants a new strategy. After one winner it wants a larger stake. Both impulses destroy the only thing you can study: the same rules, same risk percent, written down.

Twenty rows will not prove an edge. They will prove whether you can follow the rules you wrote. Most people never clear that hurdle.

Printable journal in the kit. The rule is in the post.

A daily stop only works if it is written before the session and obeyed after the third loser.

Pick a percent you can lose today without needing to make it back tonight. Two percent is a common ceiling. Write the dollar amount. When it hits, close the platform.

The extra try is how 2% becomes 8%.

Size the trade from the losing streak you do not want, not from the screenshot you do.

Five losers in a row is not rare. If those five at your current stake take 10% off the account, the stake is entertainment.

A simple ceiling: 0.5% to 1% per trade. On a $500 demo that is $2.50 to $5. It looks small. Small is the point.

A two-week plan that keeps live money off the calendar.

Days 1–3: learn the buttons.
Days 4–10: one setup, twenty journal rows.
Days 11–14: count broken rules first, results second.

If you cannot keep a daily stop on demo, you will not keep it live. Funding a live account is a separate decision and this plan does not require it.

Worked example, not a recommendation.

$500 account.
1% risk → $5 max at risk this trade.
2% daily cap → $10.
Two full-risk losers and the day is done.

If that feels too small to bother, you are looking at the wrong product. These markets will take the large number just as fast as the small one.

Sunday review, if you traded this week:

Count broken rules first.
Then wins and losses.
Then whether the daily stop was hit.

A green week with ignored stops is still a failed sample.

The weekly review sheet is page two of the journal.
